title: fix: keep local changes visible beside existing pull requests
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Environment hides local edits after a pull request is published and can show Retry beside a pull request that already exists for the current branch.

## User Impact

Local change counts remain visible and open the Uncommitted review. Existing pull requests keep their usual row without a duplicate publication offer.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Gateway owner already identifies the current checkout's pull requests, including forks, and omits unpublished branch facts when it finds a live pull request. Environment now respects that result independently of an old publication failure, while preserving recovery for an unresolved publication and actions for another unpublished branch. A publication receipt no longer suppresses separately received Uncommitted changes; an authoritative clean working tree still clears the counts.

## Evidence

- Both new browser scenarios failed on the base for the intended visible defect, then passed with the fix. The same real Details flow opens the Uncommitted review with the expected file and counts; no GitHub publication request is sent.
- Focused component tests: 19 passed; 0.838s Vitest time, 1.52s wrapper wall time. They also cover an unresolved publication, a different unpublished branch, and confirmed zero local changes.
- Production UI browser tests: 3 passed, 5.821s test time, 24.82s reported run duration. New scenarios cost 1.553s and 1.713s. Existing shared Uncommitted demand/failure recovery remains covered. CI on the integrated head: 8.607s for this three-test file; the two new scenarios took 2.864s and 2.476s.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, focused type-aware lint, formatter, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 defects.
- GitHub merged current main into the PR after a reopened event retained an obsolete merge SHA. All three product/test files remain byte-identical to the reviewed patch. Current [CI run 40107013736](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40107013736) checks integrated head `d757187800024030e5c871569cab6c6d8ef03545`, including the canonical Workboard guard fix from main. The preceding integrated run passed Environment browser tests and the performance gate: chat boot 1,274,848 B gzip against the unchanged 1,275,713 B limit; +150 B against its actual main base.

Synthetic conversation, same checkout and data before/after. Composer model labels are replaced with “Demo model”; the affected Environment and PR areas are unmodified. The video is slowed threefold for readability.

Risk and coverage: this changes only Environment presentation, with a net reduction of one production line. No additional polling, state store, protocol, permission, or GitHub mutation is introduced. Existing branch-versus-default statistics retain their semantics. This proof uses the production UI with an isolated mock Gateway; no live GitHub publication or operator Gateway was changed.
